video_title: History May Tell Us What Comes Next For Clippers + INTERESTING Signings Updates In The West

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Kawhi Leonard trade between the Raptors and Clippers has stalled
quotes.excerpt: The trade between the Raptors and the Clippers for Kawhi Leonard has not gone through.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The trade between the Raptors and the Clippers for Kawhi Leonard has not gone through.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Well again, this is Monday night. We'll see what happens on Tuesday. In talking to people, I think that trade is going to go through and I think it's going to go through as is.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer likely received support from peer owners during the investigation
quotes.excerpt: I think Steve Ballmer was getting the benefit of the doubt from his peer owners through this process.
quotes.quote: In talking to some folks, I think Steve Ballmer was getting the benefit of the doubt from his peer owners through this process. I know that there were some people who believe that he was, especially the teams that were trying to get Kawhi back in 2019 and heard out of Uncle Dennis's mouth the requests that came through here, and the teams that were impacted by Kawhi picking the Clippers, they may not have felt that way.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves had their first-round draft pick restored two days after pleading guilty
quotes.excerpt: It was two days after they pleaded guilty. The penalty came down in October and the Wolves had their first returned pick back before Christmas.
quotes.quote: It was two days after they pleaded guilty. The penalty came down in October and the Wolves had their first returned pick back before Christmas. I'll just point out that the Wolves at first were in denial. The process was different back then. They used an arbiter and not a law firm. But when the Wolves were found guilty, Glenn Taylor said words that were not I'm guilty. Kevin McHale, who was the vice president of basketball operations, said words like I didn't even know this existed. He played ignorance. They thought about it and they negotiated with the league office and they pleaded guilty. And two days after they basically they waved the white flag in December, David Stern gave them back a pick.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers ownership support for Steve Ballmer is currently non-existent
quotes.excerpt: My conversations indicate that Steve Ballmer's support among ownership is currently nil.
quotes.quote: I talked to a number of people about this and some people said that the Clippers should go on the offensive because part of the way that you get what you want is by going on the offense. And you know that that's what lawyers are for and that there's more ways to achieve negotiation than capitulation. But I'm just telling you, my conversations indicate that Steve Ballmer's support among ownership is currently nil and I can't predict what's going to happen there.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers suffered from 'little brother syndrome' in their pursuit of success
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers were guilty of the same thing that the Nets were. They had little brother syndrome.
quotes.quote: I was talking to somebody who's been around the league for a long time and he said, the Clippers were guilty of the same thing that the Nets were. They had little brother syndrome and they really tried to, they were so focused on not being the little brother anymore that they took way too big a gambles.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nets made two high-stakes gambles that failed to produce a championship
quotes.excerpt: The Nets have done it twice. The Nets did it with the KG-Pierce deal and then they did it again with the Kawhi, Kyrie, then James Harden trade.
quotes.quote: The Nets have done it twice. The Nets did it with the KG-Pierce deal and then they did it again with the Kawhi, Kyrie, then James Harden trade. Now, what I will say about the Kawhi, Kyrie, and then James Harden trade soon thereafter, that's a situation anybody who would have been in that position to do it would have absolutely have done it. And anybody who would have been in a position to get Kawhi Leonard fresh off a Finals MVP and Paul George fresh off a first-team All-NBA season, I think would have done it too.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Andrei Kirilenko opted out of a $10 million option to sign with the Nets
quotes.excerpt: Andrei Kirilenko had a 10 million dollar one-year player option. He opted out of it and shortly thereafter he signed a two-year 6 million dollar deal with the Nets.
quotes.quote: Andrei Kirilenko had a 10 million dollar one-year player option. He opted out of it and shortly thereafter he signed a two-year 6 million dollar deal with the Nets. So he left seven million on the table in the first year and four million overall. And you know, this is in 2013, you know, consider inflation, you know, it's a lot of money. And shortly after he bought the Nets and the Nets were sort of ramping up, Andrei Kirilenko, who's the greatest Russian ever in the NBA, shortly after he bought the Nets and the Nets were ramping up, Andrei Kirilenko was on the backside of his career, but he was playing in Minnesota and it was clear that Prokhorov wanted a Russian player, wanted the best Russian player.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Amen Thompson's five-year, $208 million extension is a significant commitment from the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Amen Thompson did his five-year 208 million dollar extension with the Houston Rockets.
quotes.quote: Amen Thompson did his five-year 208 million dollar extension with the Houston Rockets. Not a first couple days of September, a little bit of an unusual time to get a contract extension done, but the Rockets obviously were pleased with doing this because they've been a team that has held their ground in rookie extensions.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Rockets value Amen Thompson as one of the league's most valuable players
quotes.excerpt: If there's one untradeable player on the roster, it is him.
quotes.quote: If there's one untradeable player on the roster, it is him. According to their metrics, they think he's one of the top 10, and I might be inflating that number, most valuable players in the league.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Amen Thompson's best version is a young superstar version of Ben Simmons
quotes.excerpt: I think Amen Thompson, like the best version of him, is a young superstar version of Ben Simmons.
quotes.quote: I think Amen Thompson, like the best version of him, is a young superstar version of Ben Simmons. The best version of him offensively. Really, I think that's the best comp for him. Ben Simmons was a superstar. I'm just telling you, I think that's the kind of player that Amen Thompson can be.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Simmons was already a two-time All-Star when he signed his max contract
quotes.excerpt: When the Sixers gave Ben Simmons his max contract, he had already been a two-time All-Star.
quotes.quote: When the Sixers gave Ben Simmons his max contract, he had already been a two-time All-Star. He was rookie of the year and two-time All-Star. He already was a multi-time All-Star.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Simmons' career trajectory changed significantly after his back injury
quotes.excerpt: He was never quite the same player after that.
quotes.quote: It was a combination of clearly there was some mental blockage, there was some psychological stuff, and then the back injury. And for me, the back injury plays bigger roles than anything. Absolutely, because this is a dude who was just an extraordinarily dynamic 6-foot-10, 240-pound athlete, and then he just wasn't that same kind of athlete after he had the back issues. And I'll be honest with you, when the back issues first popped up, I thought it was BS to get his way out of Philly when he was in that standoff with the Sixers, but he held out and then had the back injury when he came back. Then he has the surgery, and honestly, nobody has back surgery just because. That's a last-ditch type of thing and he just never was the same after that.
